answer.content: IPv4 and IPv6 differ significantly in their addressing schemes and capabilities. IPv4 uses 32-bit addresses, allowing for approximately 4.3 billion unique addresses, which is running out. IPv6 employs 128-bit addresses, offering practically unlimited possibilities.  IPv4 addresses are in dotted decimal format, e.g., 192.168.1.1, while IPv6 uses hexadecimal with colons, like 2001:db8::1.  IPv4 headers include a checksum and options, making them more complex and slower, whereas IPv6 headers are simpler, having a fixed header and optional extension headers.  IPv4 relies on ARP and ICMP for addressing and error reporting, while IPv6 integrates IPsec for security and uses ICMPv6 for diagnostics.  IPv4 is connection-oriented, requiring a handshake before data transmission, whereas IPv6 is connectionless, allowing packets to be routed independently.  IPv4 has a fixed bandwidth, which can be inefficient when not all links are in use, unlike IPv6, which allocates bandwidth on demand.  IPv4 is used in older applications like HTTP, FTP, and SMTP, while IPv6 is more suitable for newer applications such as DNS, streaming, and games. [p. 2]
